cap: Theca cells, next to capillaries, use LH to turn cholesterol into androstenedione but have little aromatase. Granulosa cells, inside the basement membrane, use FSH-induced aromatase to convert that androgen into estrone and estradiol. Neither cell can make estradiol alone, which is why a follicle needs both gonadotropins. Aromatase in fat performs the same conversion outside the ovary and makes estrone, the main estrogen after menopause.
teach: LH acts on the theca cell to raise desmolase, which converts cholesterol to pregnenolone; this first step is rate limiting for every steroid hormone. Pregnenolone is then converted to androstenedione and some testosterone. The granulosa cell, equipped with aromatase by FSH, converts androstenedione to estrone and testosterone to estradiol. After ovulation, capillaries invade the granulosa layer and the luteinized cells can take up LDL cholesterol and make progesterone.
